$comment: Single source of truth for every directory in this repository that is vendored from an upstream project. scripts/sync_vendor.py reads this file to perform both the initial import and every scheduled refresh, so an import and an update take exactly the same code path. Do not hand-edit vendored directories: change the manifest, then re-run the script. A source maps a list of upstream subtrees into its own vendored root, preserving the relative distance between them so links inside the vendored content keep resolving. kind=skill-collection tracks each child directory individually; kind=support copies a linked-into subtree whole.

sources.name: pstack
sources.author: Lauren Tan (@backnotprop, "poteto")

exclude_reasons.tdd: Frontmatter name collides with the local skills/engineering/tdd. The local skill is the canonical one for this repository.
exclude_reasons.teach: Frontmatter name collides with the local skills/productivity/teach.
exclude_reasons.reflect: Frontmatter name collides with the local skills/productivity/reflect/skills/reflect.
exclude_reasons.bro: Requires the external backnotprop/bro repository at runtime. Out of scope for an offline-first skills library; add it as its own manifest source if that dependency is ever accepted.

sources.mandatory_reason: unslop is an always-apply writing-quality skill and is a required import for this repository. The sync script fails if a mandatory skill is missing from the upstream tree or has been excluded.
limitations: poteto-mode, setup-pstack and arena assume a Cursor-style multi-model runner. The engineering discipline in them is portable; the model names (sol, grok, fable, opus 5) are not.

Upstream names the poteto-mode skill `Poteto Mode`, which fails this repository's SK004 and SK005 metadata rules. It is reported as a warning rather than corrected, because correcting it would fork the file.
sources.notes: Vendored verbatim under a dedicated namespace so upstream refreshes are a mechanical diff. Everything upstream keeps under skills/ is self-contained, so this source needs only one mapped path.

sources.name: job-hunt-skills
sources.author: Remotivated
limitations: DOCX and PDF export is not vendored. `scripts/export-documents.mjs` needs a checked-in 1.9 MB Node dependency bundle plus a pinned Typst binary, and this repository has no Node CI to keep either honest. Everything the skills do in Markdown works without it. For ATS-safe DOCX and PDF output, clone the upstream repository and run it there.

`scripts/scaffold-state.mjs` and `scripts/profile-strength.mjs` ARE vendored. Both import only `node:fs`, `node:path` and `node:url`, so they run on any Node 18+ with nothing installed. They are vendored because `get-started` calls the scaffolder its "Preferred" path and `_shared/state-layer.md` says the skills run it; omitting them guaranteed a file-not-found for anyone following the primary instruction.

The skills expect a `my-documents/` state layer in the user's own working directory, described in `skills/_shared/state-layer.md`. That is the user's data and is deliberately not vendored. Run the `get-started` skill to create it.

`skills/_shared/` holds a shared instruction contract rather than a skill, so it carries no SKILL.md and is exempt from the per-skill provenance rule. It is imported and provenance-stamped as a shared support directory.

Upstream's own contributor checks (`check-internal-links.py`, `test_skill_contracts.py`, the export tests) are not vendored. Link integrity of the vendored subset is instead enforced here by `scripts/check_links.py` in CI.
sources.notes: The upstream skills carry 47 links to ../_shared/state-layer.md and further links to ../../guides/ and templates/. Copying only skills/ would leave every one of those links pointing at nothing, so guides/, templates/ and the two dependency-free helper scripts are mapped alongside at the same relative distance and the links resolve unchanged. This is why a manifest source declares a list of paths rather than one subdirectory.
